generationContext.text:
# Microsoft Azure Batch management client library for .NET

Use Microsoft Azure Batch to run large-scale parallel and high-performance computing (HPC) batch jobs efficiently in Azure. Azure Batch creates and manages a pool of compute nodes (virtual machines), installs the applications you want to run, and schedules jobs to run on the nodes. 

This library supports managing Microsoft Azure Batch resources.

This library follows the [new Azure SDK guidelines](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/general_introduction.html), and provides many core capabilities:

    - Support MSAL.NET, Azure.Identity is out of box for supporting MSAL.NET.
    - Support [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) for distributed tracing.
    - HTTP pipeline with custom policies.
    - Better error-handling.
    - Support uniform telemetry across all languages.

## Getting started 

### Install the package

Install the Microsoft Azure Batch management library for .NET with [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/):

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.ResourceManager.Batch
```

### Prerequisites

* You must have an [Microsoft Azure subscription](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/dotnet/).

### Authenticate the Client

To create an authenticated client and start interacting with Microsoft Azure resources, see the [quickstart guide here](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).

## Key concepts

Key concepts of the Microsoft Azure SDK for .NET can be found [here](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/dotnet_introduction.html).

## Documentation

Documentation is available to help you learn how to use this package:

- [Quickstart](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).
- [API References](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/?view=azure-dotnet).
- [Authentication](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/identity/Azure.Identity/README.md).

## Examples

Code samples for using the management library for .NET can be found in the following locations
- [.NET Management Library Code Samples](https://aka.ms/azuresdk-net-mgmt-samples)

## Troubleshooting

-   File an issue via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/issues).
-   Check [previous questions](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/azure+.net) or ask new ones on Stack Overflow using Azure and .NET tags.

## Next steps

For more information about Microsoft Azure SDK, see [this website](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/).

## Contributing

For details on contributing to this repository, see the [contributing
guide][cg].

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions
require you to agree to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) declaring
that you have the right to, and actually do, grant us the rights to use
your contribution. For details, visit <https://cla.microsoft.com>.

When you submit a pull request, a CLA-bot will automatically determine
whether you need to provide a CLA and decorate the PR appropriately
(for example, label, comment). Follow the instructions provided by the
bot. You'll only need to do this action once across all repositories
using our CLA.

This project has adopted the [Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct][coc]. For
more information, see the [Code of Conduct FAQ][coc_faq] or contact
<opencode@microsoft.com> with any other questions or comments.

proposals.subtype: Hidden pool factory unwraps a deployment configuration
proposals.explanation: The overload accepting BatchDeploymentConfiguration extracts VmConfiguration and forwards to a named-argument factory call, supplying null tags, taskSchedulingPolicy and upgradePolicy. Certificates, applicationLicenses, taskSchedulingNodeFillType and both node-communication-mode parameters are not forwarded.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: An implemented hidden overload is captured in src/Custom outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Hidden pool factory forwards a VM configuration with null scheduling policy
proposals.explanation: The optional-argument overload forwards deploymentVmConfiguration, tags and upgradePolicy and supplies null taskSchedulingPolicy. The supplied body does not forward certificates, applicationLicenses, either node-communication mode, taskSchedulingNodeFillType or resourceTags.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The explicit parameter-adaptation body is in the non-generated Custom factory.

decisions.reason: The Custom factory overload at lines 60-98 extracts VmConfiguration and forwards the listed arguments while omitting the named legacy parameters; this is an implemented, hidden compatibility overload, not a generated poller.

The second non-generated overload at lines 101-138 passes deploymentVmConfiguration, tags and upgradePolicy, supplies a null scheduling policy, and does not pass the other parameters identified; its signature is distinct from the preceding overload.

The hidden obsolete factory in Custom source takes certificate data arguments but constructs the parameterless data model at lines 141-146; the compatibility-stub classification is supported without assuming why it was retained.
The separately named obsolete content factory takes input arguments and returns a parameterless content model at lines 149-154; this is a distinct handwritten model-factory compatibility stub.

The non-generated factory body at lines 157-162 defaults tags and wraps value in DetectorResponseProperties. The model-factory pattern and plausible generator addressability describe the reusable shape, not a proven generator capability.
Lines 165-170 explicitly initialize missing tags and construct ApplicationProperties from the stated flattened arguments in a handwritten Custom factory.
Lines 173-178 of the non-generated factory default tags and wrap the supplied package fields in ApplicationPackageProperties.
Lines 181-188 default collections, conditionally construct PrivateEndpoint, and adapt groupIds to a list inside the non-generated factory.
The Custom factory at lines 191-198 supplies default lists and tags and constructs the nested private-link properties model.
Both non-generated certificate-creation signatures at lines 34-47 synchronously throw NotSupportedException; the ArmOperation return type does not establish any polling behavior.
The collection's Get and GetAsync bodies at lines 52-61 are handwritten unsupported-operation stubs preserving separate read signatures.
The pageable signatures at lines 68-79 both immediately throw; the proposal correctly does not count them as pagination.
The collection's separate existence-check signatures at lines 84-93 throw before producing a boolean; they implement the stated handwritten unsupported-operation behavior.
The GetIfExists pair at lines 98-107 returns no nullable response and instead throws; this distinct optional-read API is a compatibility stub.
All three explicit enumerator implementations at lines 109-116 throw immediately in the handwritten collection, so the finding concerns unsupported enumeration, not working iteration.

Lines 20-61 define a substantive obsolete model with declared properties and a constructor initializing Tags in non-generated Custom source; the stated lack of other assignments is scoped to the shown constructor.
The hidden obsolete Thumbprint property's handwritten getter and setter at lines 66-72 perform the described BinaryData/string conversion, a distinct model accessor.

The source implements no serialization: its read/write hooks throw, and the format hook only returns J. This is an unsupported persistence compatibility interface, not a custom serializer, so Other is more specific to its actual purpose than Serialization.

finding.explanation: The certificate model's JsonModelWriteCore and IJsonModel/IPersistableModel Create and Write methods throw NotSupportedException; GetFormatFromOptions returns J without implementing a JSON codec.
finding.handwrittenRationale: These concrete interface and override bodies occur in src/Custom/BatchAccountCertificateData.cs outside Generated.

decisions.reason: The obsolete resource's non-generated Data getter throws and HasData is false at lines 34-37; this is an observable resource-data compatibility behavior, not model deserialization.

The handwritten static helper at lines 40-44 builds an ARM path and a ResourceIdentifier. Generator addressability is plausible for this structural helper, not proof that this generator currently emits it.
The resource's Get/GetAsync bodies at lines 48-56 each immediately throw, unlike the separate collection read methods.
Delete/DeleteAsync at lines 61-70 throw despite their ArmOperation signatures; there is no handwritten LRO implementation in these bodies.
The distinct Update/UpdateAsync signatures at lines 76-86 are handwritten stubs that throw instead of sending the supplied content.
The resource's CancelDeletion pair at lines 90-98 throws before any request, a distinct unsupported operation in Custom source.
AddTag and AddTagAsync at lines 104-114 both throw; no tag mutation is implemented in the supplied bodies.
SetTags and SetTagsAsync at lines 119-128 both throw in non-generated Custom source rather than applying a replacement tag set.
RemoveTag and RemoveTagAsync at lines 133-142 immediately throw, independently of the add/set tag signatures.

The resource does not serialize or deserialize model data: every Create/Write body throws and only the format hook returns J. Categorize this compatibility interface as Other rather than a working Serialization customization.

finding.explanation: The certificate resource's IJsonModel and IPersistableModel Create and Write methods throw NotSupportedException; GetFormatFromOptions returns J without implementing a JSON codec.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The explicit interface bodies are in src/Custom/BatchAccountCertificateResource.cs outside Generated.

omissions.explanation: The handwritten obsolete certificate resource exposes a public static ResourceType constant for Microsoft.Batch/batchAccounts/certificates separately from its resource-identifier helper.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: The public field declaration occurs in src/Custom/BatchAccountCertificateResource.cs outside Generated; whether an equivalent declaration exists in uncaptured generated source is unknown.

limitations: Four of 420 eligible files are captured and twenty-one paths are explicitly skipped. This is bounded discovery, not package-wide completeness.
The supplied certificate-management deprecation messages are source facts, not independent verification that an API was removed from the deployed service or a historical release.
Certificate compatibility signatures that throw or return empty parameterless models are not counted as working LRO, paging, serialization or service operations.
Generated pool factory implementations and historical API contracts are absent. Unforwarded parameters are observed call-site facts; no alternate preservation or build/runtime outcome is inferred.

Public certificate auto-members and their basic Tags initialization are assessed as one handwritten model contract, with its binary projection and persistence stubs assessed separately; empty protected constructors are not additional findings.
Source version 1.8.0-beta.1 differs from latest-release metadata 1.7.0; the source version is not proof of publication.

Only four of 420 eligible files were captured (458 discovered; 21 named Custom files skipped for the review budget); the supplied subset cannot establish package-wide absence or a complete customization count.

Generated counterparts, the referenced factory overload, and the unprovided certificate content model are not captured. The forwarding, public API compatibility and omission judgments are limited to the shown bodies and signatures; an omission is a candidate, not an accepted finding.

Handwritten-marker classification and paths under src/Custom support provenance of the captured bodies, but no compiled public API or generator output was independently compared. Generator addressability is plausibility only, not verified generator capability.

The certificate APIs are marked obsolete/hidden and throw; their retained signatures do not prove that the current Batch service supports the operations or that any pagination, LRO polling or JSON serialization occurs.
